analysis.title: Economic Outlook and Investment Strategy, November 2026
key_insights: BJSS sees global growth peaking and moderating in 2027, with most major economies still above potential. The slowdown reflects a fading AI capex impulse and tighter macro policy.

Inflation is expected to peak in 1Q27 on reduced slack and elevated energy prices, assuming no new crude spikes. Central banks are expected to hike several times in 2027, with rates peaking in Q2-Q3 and some easing in 2028.

Fed forecast: one hike in December and three more in 2027, taking the upper bound of the Fed Funds range to 5% by Q3 2027. Taylor rules suggest the policy rate should be well above the Fed's own projections.

ECB expected to hike 25bp in December and once more in Q1 2027, taking the deposit rate to 3%. BoE to hike in December and once more in 2027, BoJ to hike in December and twice in 1H27, SNB to hike 25bp in both March and June 2027 to 0.50%.
US GDP 2027 forecast raised to 2.3% (from 2.1%) per the main-changes box, and US CPI 2027 to 2.9% (from 2.7%). The forecast table lists US GDP at 2.4% in 2026, 2.1% in 2027 and 1.9% in 2028.

US consumers are resilient despite falling real labour income, supported by a wealth effect. The payroll breakeven rate is estimated near 30,000 versus 100,000 historically, so unemployment has fallen despite weak job creation.

AI is adding to US inflation mainly through indirect effects and strong domestic spending, while higher IT product prices have a limited impact. Higher gasoline prices and services ISM prices paid point to higher headline inflation by year end.
Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are back to pre-war levels, but transport costs have surged, leaving a large transportation risk premium in crude.

China 2026 growth forecast raised to 4.6% (from 4.5%) and 2027 held at 4.5% in the table. Strong exports and improving fiscal execution support growth, though local officials are expected to stay cautious ahead of the 2027 political transition.

Euro area Q3 GDP grew 0.4% qoq and 1.3% yoy. Inflation is picking up on import prices and a halt to wage disinflation. Wider French bond spreads are not expected to trigger a crisis given bank solidity and ECB readiness, though French debt-to-GDP is 30 points above the euro area average.
Japan operates above capacity, inflation expectations have breached 2%, and main inflation measures crossed 2% in September. Inflation is expected to stay above 2% in 2027.

Fixed income: long yields expected to move sideways, with carry the main driver of returns. BJSS prefers 5- to 7-year maturities, is slightly underweight bonds overall, and is neutral on credit. Credit spreads are expected to widen more over coming quarters but not enough to justify a structural underweight.
Long-term real rates are the highest in close to 20 years, and term premium normalisation is described as well advanced. High real yields are gradually tightening US financial conditions.

FX: USD supported by US cyclical strength and a hawkish Fed. EUR faces headwinds, CHF stays soft near term before SNB hikes, GBP softens on weak growth, JPY continues to rebound on BoJ hike signals. Net speculative yen positioning has turned long for the first time since early 2025.

Gold has held up well, but BJSS sees near-term downside risk from rate headwinds. It expects the metal to regain momentum further out, with PBoC buying more than 20 tonnes in July-September, its largest since 2023. Gold forecast is $4,400 by Jun-27 and $5,000 by Dec-28.

Equities: BJSS downgrades tech to neutral and cuts its end-2027 S&P 500 target to 8,500, saying double-digit returns are increasingly unlikely. Remains slightly overweight equities, with preference for Swiss and US equities, utilities and staples.

Equity risks cited: wider spreads for lower-rated credit and Neocloud AI spenders, hyperscaler free cash flow turning negative in Q3, peaking macro data and EPS growth, AI weighing on legacy earnings (Google search, Intel PC demand), and a hiking Fed.

AI financing is entering a more fragile phase, with AI debt issuance up sharply in 2026 and likely to double again in 2027. Business AI spending has flatlined despite rising token usage because token prices fell sharply in Q3.
Hyperscaler capex keeps rising in 2027 but more slowly, so the GDP stimulus fades. Earnings upgrades have peaked and US bank lending conditions have started tightening after the rise in CCC spreads.

BJSS notes valuations may have peaked without index levels peaking, citing the 2004 valuation peak that preceded an October 2007 index peak. It expects the US forward P/E to trend toward the 16.7x 20-year average by end-2027.

Anthropic IPO is expected by BJSS to follow the typical post-IPO pattern of early strength and weakness over the following year, as with SpaceX. Median returns for the top-10 largest US IPOs since 2010 are +10.3% at 1 month and -29.0% at 1 year.
BJSS is building more quality exposure, which tends to do well when growth falls and inflation rises, and has underperformed over the past six months.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth is still strong per BJSS, but GDP and EPS growth rates are expected to slow in coming quarters.
Global net earnings revisions show the 2026 upgrade cycle rolling over, with softening momentum across sectors.
Hyperscaler quarterly free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026 while capex is still increasing.
BJSS expects soft Q3 reporting from banks.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BJSS expects moderation as the AI capex impulse fades and policy tightens.
Inflation seen peaking in 1Q27 on energy prices and reduced slack.
Growth holds despite energy prices and political uncertainty.
Import prices and halted wage disinflation push inflation up.
Growth has held up well despite elevated energy prices.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US and Swiss equities, utilities and staples within equities, slight overweight equities overall
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings outlook remains positive, fiscal stimulus is supportive, and defensives hedge risks from inflation and hawkish central banks.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated inflation and hawkish central banks.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer 5- to 7-year government bond maturities, slight underweight fixed income
trade_ideas.rationale: Best risk/return trade-off, with carry the main driver of returns.
trade_ideas.risk: Further rises in policy rate expectations, particularly in the US.

trade_ideas.rationale: Infrastructure benefits from AI capex build-out while private credit struggles with recent defaults and potentially higher rates.

trade_ideas.description: EURCHF as the cleanest expression of euro area fiscal and sovereign risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Fiscal concerns in the euro area are a latent support for the franc.

risk_factors: Elevated inflation and hawkish central banks.
Hyperscaler free cash flow turning negative and rising debt funding needs.
Widening credit spreads in CCC and Neocloud segments and stress in private credit.
Peaking macro data and slowing EPS growth.
Renewed spikes in crude oil prices.
Disappointment over AI profitability could trigger capital outflows and weigh on the dollar.
vol_and_positioning: Net speculative yen positioning has turned long for the first time since early 2025, after August FX interventions and the BoJ's hawkish shift in September.
OIS-implied cumulative Fed hikes over the next 12 months fell between 30 September and 29 October, a retracement that outpaced other G10 currencies and stalled the dollar rebound.
BJSS keeps defensive hedges in place within equities.
geopolitical: Timely resolution of the Iran conflict is unlikely and the US government will likely stay gridlocked after the Midterms.
Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to pre-war levels but transport costs have surged.
De-dollarisation is expected to continue as a gradual long-term shift rather than a regime break.
French budget crisis and public finances pressure the euro and widen French-German yield spreads.
China's 2027 political transition makes local government officials cautious.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings outlook is positive, macro indicators are robust, fiscal stimulus in the US, Germany and Japan is supportive, and equity trends are intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit spreads are widening for CCC and Neocloud issuers, hyperscaler free cash flow is negative, earnings upgrades have peaked, and the Fed is hiking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further widening of CCC and Neocloud credit spreads and tighter bank lending conditions, which BJSS links to a slowdown in ISM.

tension_points.bull_case: High real yields are tightening financial conditions and term premium normalisation is well advanced, which sets up lower yields in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI capex boom and elevated inflation risk higher policy rate expectations, particularly in the US.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed spikes in crude oil prices that push inflation higher than the Q1 2027 peak BJSS assumes.
